title: Frictionless OS command injection via explore console command
affected: Frictionless stable versions before 5.19.1 and prerelease 5.20.0rc1
description: A malicious datapackage.json can inject shell commands through resource paths passed to os.system by frictionless explore, enabling arbitrary command execution with the user's privileges.

details.label: Component / Credit
details.value: frictionless.console.commands.explore - Discovered by Sai Teja Erukude, coordinated through VulnCheck.

details.label: Impact
details.value: Arbitrary command execution can compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data accessible to the user, including local files and analysis workflows.

details.label: Remediation
details.value: Upgrade to 5.19.1 or later on the stable branch, or 5.20.0rc2 or later on the prerelease branch. The fix replaces shell execution with subprocess.run using a list of arguments, so resource paths are treated as literal arguments.

title: SpeechBrain arbitrary code execution via CKPT.yaml parsing
description: Unsafe parsing of checkpoint metadata could allow crafted CKPT.yaml files to execute arbitrary Python code during Checkpointer.recover_if_possible() candidate discovery, even when the malicious checkpoint is not selected for recovery.

details.label: Component / Credit
details.value: Checkpointer.recover_if_possible() checkpoint discovery - Discovered by Sai Teja Erukude, coordinated through VulnCheck.

details.label: Impact
details.value: PyYAML's unsafe loader processes attacker-controlled CKPT.yaml metadata while enumerating checkpoint candidates. Python object construction tags can execute arbitrary code in the application process even if the malicious checkpoint is never selected for recovery, compromising its data and availability.

details.label: Remediation
details.value: Upgrade to SpeechBrain 1.1.1 or later. The referenced patch uses a safe YAML loader for checkpoint metadata to prevent arbitrary Python object construction.

title: uproot code injection via TStreamerInfo metadata

facts.label: Vector
facts.value: Local file - No privileges - User opens crafted file

description: Crafted ROOT-file metadata could be interpolated into dynamically generated Python source, enabling code execution when an affected application processes the file.

details.label: Component / Credit
details.value: ROOT TStreamerInfo reader code generation - Discovered by Sai Teja Erukude; CVE assigned by VulnCheck.

details.label: Impact
details.value: File-controlled streamer fields, such as element names, are inserted into generated Python source without safe quoting. A crafted ROOT file can inject expressions that execute when the generated reader is invoked, allowing arbitrary Python code execution with the privileges of the application opening the file.

details.label: Remediation
details.value: Upgrade to uproot 5.7.5 or later, including in applications that depend on uproot. Apply the patch referenced in the CVE record to address unsafe quoting in generated Python source.

title: Python StateMachine remote code execution via SCXML evaluation
description: Unsafe evaluation of attacker-controlled SCXML expressions could allow arbitrary Python code execution in applications that process untrusted SCXML content.

details.label: Component / Credit
details.value: SCXMLProcessor expression evaluation - Discovered by Sai Teja Erukude, coordinated through VulnCheck.

details.label: Impact
details.value: Malicious SCXML documents can supply crafted <data expr="..."> attributes. SCXMLProcessor passes those expressions to Python's eval() without sandboxing, allowing arbitrary code execution in the hosting process. The CVE rates this as a network attack requiring no privileges or user interaction.

details.label: Remediation
details.value: Upgrade Python StateMachine from affected versions 3.0.0 through 3.1.x to 3.2.0 or later. The CVE record links the fixed release and the vendor's security advisory.

title: OpenMed unauthenticated remote code execution
description: A model-loading path could allow an unauthenticated attacker to trigger execution of attacker-controlled Python code in the OpenMed service process.

details.label: Component / Credit
details.value: PII privacy-filter model loading - Discovered by Sai Teja Erukude, coordinated through VulnCheck.

details.label: Impact
details.value: Broad substring matching on model_name can route an attacker-controlled Hugging Face repository into a loader using trust_remote_code=True. Custom Transformers code declared through auto_map in config.json or tokenizer_config.json is then imported and executed with the OpenMed service's privileges, without authentication or user interaction.

details.label: Remediation
details.value: Upgrade OpenMed to 1.5.2 or later. The CVE record references the fixed release, the pull request, and the patch for the PII model-loading path.
